item.name: iPhone 18 Pro
item.summary: A spatial prototype of how a phone stores energy, processes signals and produces light, images, sound and touch.

components.name: Front cover
components.howItsMade: The cover protects the display while letting its light reach your eyes. Glass and the OLED underneath have different jobs and different optical behavior.
funFacts: A transparent cover can protect pixels without producing light itself.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: OLED display
components.material: Glass substrate and OLED stack; schematic backing
components.howItsMade: Pixels turn electrical signals into light. This opaque display panel sits beneath the separate transparent cover; it is not a piece of clear glass.
funFacts: Emit controlled light for the image you see.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Rear closure
components.material: Ceramic Shield back; illustrative colored finish
components.howItsMade: The rear closure seals the back of the device. Its colored finish blocks the view inside, even though the substrate is glass.
funFacts: Close the rear while leaving the camera optics exposed.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Stored energy
components.material: Lithium-ion battery; schematic pack and casing
components.howItsMade: Chemical energy becomes electrical power for the phone. The logic board regulates and distributes that power to its other systems.
funFacts: Supply electrical energy to the power circuitry.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Light becomes data
components.material: Optics, sensor packages and housings; schematic
components.howItsMade: Lenses focus incoming light onto sensors. The logic board then processes the sensor signals into an image; the optical path and the data path are different parts of the same story.
funFacts: Convert incoming light into electronic image signals.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Front-facing camera
components.howItsMade: A front-facing sensor captures light for calls and selfies. This model does not reconstruct the separate Face ID system.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Processing & power
components.material: Circuit board, package and shield approximations
components.howItsMade: Electronic circuits process inputs and drive outputs. Follow the connections: battery power comes in, camera data is processed, and display information goes out.
funFacts: Coordinate computation, power distribution and peripheral signals.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Motion you can feel
components.howItsMade: Electrical input produces controlled mechanical vibration. The enclosure transmits that vibration to your hand; this housing does not yet show the moving mechanism inside.
funFacts: Produce tactile feedback through controlled movement.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Top speaker
components.howItsMade: Convert electrical signals into sound. Manufacturing details are unresolved.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Sound output
components.howItsMade: A speaker converts an electrical signal into moving air. Its enclosure and outlet shape the sound; those acoustic paths still need a detailed reconstruction.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Power & data in
components.material: Illustrative metal shell and insulating tongue
components.howItsMade: The port connects the phone to wired power and data. Its shell protects the connector; electrical contacts carry the signals and power.
funFacts: Provide a wired connection for charging and data.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

components.name: Structure around it all
components.material: Aluminum; exact alloy and finish unverified
components.howItsMade: The enclosure gives the assembly its shape and supports its parts. It also provides interfaces for controls and openings; small seals and fasteners are omitted here.
funFacts: Support and protect the phone’s assemblies.
components.figureLabel: Approximate geometry; verify against exact-model views.

evidence.note: Component role is educational; placement, shape and finish are not reference-matched.

references.title: Apple technical specifications

references.limitations: Does not establish exact internal meshes, hidden materials or factory CAD.

references.observation: Read the component/procedure inventory and regional eSIM/pSIM and antenna distinctions in the table of contents.
references.limitations: Linked internal-view and procedure pages returned HTTP 429 during this audit. Their diagrams were not inspected; do not treat this inventory as observed internal geometry.
